_about: Water (1) + ethanol (2): excess molar enthalpy at 423.2 K and 5000 kPa, binary data set from Fang et al. (2014). Rows as in the ThermoML Archive record: mole fraction of water, excess molar enthalpy in kJ/mol (as printed). Used as an independent check of the excess enthalpy predicted by the activity models (the ethanol + water parameters were fitted to vapour-liquid data only).

source.citation: G. S. Fang, K. Tsukamoto, M. Maebayashi, M. Ohba, H. Ogawa, Excess enthalpy for the (benzene + cyclohexane) mixture over a wide range of temperature and pressure, J. Chem. Thermodyn. 78 (2014) 204-214
source.access: Journal article is subscription-only; the same data is public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive (NIST open license).
source.tables: ThermoML record, first data set: compounds 1 water + 2 ethanol, excess molar enthalpy, variable mole fraction of compound 1 (water), constraints T = 423.2 K and P = 5000 kPa. The table number in the article was not checked (article not open).

notes: Expanded uncertainties (95 %) in the record: 0.015 kJ/mol at x_1 = 0.1473 down to 0.0112 kJ/mol at x_1 = 0.9673. The record also holds sets at 423.2 K / 15000 kPa and 523.2 K / 15000 kPa (not transcribed; at 523.2 K ethanol is above its critical temperature). Read twice from the ThermoML Archive (XML and JSON files), both reads identical for this set; the XML gives the mole fraction as that of compound 1, water. To be checked by a person against the record before use (AGENTS.md rule 4).
